application_credentials.description:
The integration signs in through its own published Cloudflare OAuth client, so nothing needs adding here.

A credential entered here replaces the built-in client with [one of your own]({docs_oauth_clients}). Create it under Manage Account → OAuth clients with redirect URL `{redirect_uri}`, grant types authorization code and refresh token, token endpoint authentication none (PKCE) and the scopes {scopes}, then enter its client ID with an empty secret. The [project notes]({more_info_url}) walk through it.

user.title: Cloudflare Access
user.description:
Cloudflare Access will guard the whole hostname: people with a Home Assistant account log in through Access, and voice assistants or MCP clients obtain their tokens from it.

The next page signs you in with Cloudflare; its consent page lists the permissions the integration uses.

A desktop browser is required: the Android companion app cannot complete the return from the consent page.

account.title: Cloudflare account
account.description: The sign-in covers several accounts. Choose the one whose zone serves the hostname.

api_token.title: Cloudflare API token
api_token.description: An account-level token with the permissions 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' and 'Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups: Read'. The integration stores it in the config entry.

settings.title: Hostname and options
settings.description: The gate starts off, so nothing changes at the edge until you enable it in the options.

The lifetime of an [Access session]({docs_session}) before the person logs in again.

A registered client's refresh token lives as long.
data_description.delete_objects_on_remove:
Removal of the integration also removes its Access applications.

Switched off, the applications stay in Cloudflare, e.g. for another instance to adopt.

people.name: People
people.description: Access grants entry to every person with an e-mail address below. A person whose login username is an address needs nothing; anyone else needs an address typed here, and stays out while it is empty.{no_address_note}

bypass.name: Bypass policies
bypass.description: Bypass policies let requests through without a login. They serve callers that hold neither the login cookie nor a token, such as a third-party service posting to a webhook or a media player fetching audio by URL. Nothing is open unless listed here.

data_description.extra_bypass_paths:
Path prefixes reachable without a login, each an [Access bypass policy]({docs_policies}).

The list offers what this Home Assistant serves; any prefix can be typed.
data_description.service_token_ids:
Client IDs of [Access service tokens]({docs_service_tokens}) that pass the gate.

Your own scripts on other machines use these.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in with Cloudflare again
reauth_confirm.description: Cloudflare no longer accepts the sign-in. The next page signs you in again.

restart_required.title: Restart Home Assistant to accept clients authenticated by Cloudflare Access
restart_required.description: The integration was set up after the web server had started, so its authentication middleware could not be installed. Until a restart, Home Assistant rejects the requests of token-bearing clients (Google Assistant, Alexa, MCP clients) that Cloudflare Access admitted.

no_allowed_users.title: No Home Assistant user can pass the Cloudflare Access gate
no_allowed_users.description:
No person has an e-mail address any more, so the gate's allow policy has nobody to list; it keeps its last subjects.

Enter an address under the integration's options, People, or [change a username]({docs_change_username}) to the address.

user.title: OAuth client
user.description:
A client that logs people in through Access and calls Home Assistant with the token: an MCP client such as Claude, Google Home account linking, the Alexa skill.

The callback URL comes from the client's side.

A client that [registers itself]({docs_managed_oauth}) needs nothing more. A console that asks for a client ID and secret receives them on the next page, from [an Access application of its own]({docs_saas_apps}).

data_description.needs_credentials: On for a console that asks for a client ID and secret (Google Home, Alexa); off for a client that registers itself (MCP).
